established_findings.statement: LLMs can translate intent or generate draft network configurations, but they frequently produce syntax/semantic/topology errors unless combined with deterministic verification or localized feedback.
limitations: Evaluations typically use limited topologies or curated tasks rather than broad production deployments
Model and prompt diversity in cited works is limited (not exhaustive across all LLMs)
Human-in-the-loop involvement varies across studies and affects results

established_findings.statement: Benchmarks of LLM-driven configuration repair (Cornetto) report that LLMs can suggest fixes but often introduce regressions and degrade at larger scale; agentic architectures augmented with verification/tools improve repair efficacy and safety on these benchmarks.
limitations: Cornetto scenarios are synthesized; real-world heterogeneity may differ
Reported percent improvements (agentic vs base) are benchmark-specific and may not generalize to all deployments
Exact model versions and prompt recipes vary across evaluated LLMs

established_findings.statement: Hybrid generate–verify–repair workflows that combine LLM generation with formal/deterministic validators or focused fault-localization materially reduce unsafe or incorrect repairs compared to raw LLM outputs.
limitations: Cross-domain transferability (e.g., from program repair to network configs) is plausible but not identical
Scalability and runtime cost of repeated verification loops are not uniformly characterized
Quality of the verifier/specification strongly conditions success

established_findings.statement: The literature contains multiple recent surveys and reviews identifying promise of LLMs for NetOps/AIOps while consistently flagging hallucination, calibration, domain-shift, and verification as primary risks to operational trustworthiness.
limitations: Surveys summarize diverse primary studies with varying methodologies
Rapid field evolution means new results may postdate these surveys

established_findings.statement: Agentic/multi-agent LLM architectures and tool-use frameworks (retrieval, verifiers, orchestration) are actively explored and, in benchmarked cases, help manage context and iterative validation to improve repair outcomes.
limitations: Improvements depend on specific orchestration designs and available tools
Evidence is primarily from benchmarks and prototypes rather than large-scale production systems

unresolved_questions.statement: How reliably do LLM-driven repair or generation pipelines generalize to heterogeneous, production-scale network topologies and live operational constraints?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: benchmark / system reports highlight but do not resolve
limitations: Benchmarks show scale-related degradation but do not fully cover production diversity
Real-world deployment studies remain sparse in the supplied records

unresolved_questions.statement: What are effective, empirically validated defenses against prompt-injection or adversarial inputs targeting LLM-based NetOps agents specifically?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: security / adversarial literature indicates risk but domain-specific mitigations are unsettled
limitations: Existing adversarial studies are general or NLP-focused; few target NetOps workflows directly
Operational defenses require integration with verification and governance layers yet to be widely evaluated

unresolved_questions.statement: Can LLMs provide calibrated, reliable confidence estimates or trust metrics adequate for automated NetOps decision gates without external verification?
limitations: Calibration work is shown in other domains (forecasting, governance metrics) but not validated as sufficient alone for high-risk NetOps actions
Metrics and thresholds for operational acceptance remain to be standardized

candidate_gaps.statement: A standardized, publicly available benchmark suite combining large-scale real-network topologies, heterogeneous device vendors, and formal verification oracles for LLM-driven NetOps tasks is still needed beyond current synthesized datasets.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: benchmark / gap identified by recent work
limitations: Cornetto and NetConfEval advance benchmarking but rely on synthesized or limited-real-data scenarios
Creating such a benchmark has operational and privacy challenges

candidate_gaps.statement: Systematic studies comparing multi-model LLM ensembles, agentic orchestration styles, and verifier designs on common, realistic NetOps workloads are sparse in the supplied record set.
limitations: Some benchmark papers evaluate multiple models, but comprehensive comparative design-space studies are limited
Resource costs for broad multi-model experiments are high

candidate_gaps.statement: Operational governance tooling (semantic tracing, auditability, human-review gating) integrated end-to-end with LLM-based NetOps agents lacks broad empirical validation in production-like settings.
limitations: Prototypes and frameworks exist, but evidence of efficacy at production scale is limited in the supplied records
Human–machine workflow studies are underrepresented

excluded_claims: LLMs are production-ready to autonomously perform unrestricted network configuration and repair without deterministic verification (not supported by supplied records).
LLMs never introduce regressions when used for network configuration repair (contradicted by Cornetto and related evaluations).
Any single study here demonstrates comprehensive, real-world production deployment and certification of LLM-driven NetOps (no supplied record provides such evidence).
Claims of being the first-ever work to apply LLMs to NetOps in general (novelty 'first' assertions) are not supported by the supplied literature, which includes multiple prior and contemporary works.
